name: Learning from the shape and structure of data
gist: Papers that use geometric and topological ideas like symmetries, manifolds, and higher-dimensional shapes to help models understand data structure more deeply.
explain: Beyond just connections, data often has hidden structure—symmetries, shapes, patterns that repeat in predictable ways. A molecule looks the same if you rotate it or reflect it, so the model should learn the same representation regardless of how the atoms are drawn on paper, because the molecule hasn't changed. A social network has community structure: groups of people who are tightly connected internally but loosely connected to other groups. High-dimensional data often lives on lower-dimensional manifolds, curved surfaces in space. These geometric and topological ideas—which is fancy language for 'symmetries and shapes'—can help models learn more efficiently because the model doesn't waste capacity learning the same pattern multiple times.

The challenge is that standard neural networks don't inherently respect these symmetries and structures. If you rotate a molecule's coordinates, the model might give a different answer even though the molecule didn't change. This wastes the model's learning capacity: it has to learn the same pattern multiple times for each rotation. Similarly, if you know data lives on a 2D surface in 3D space, treating it as full 3D data is wasteful.

Researchers tackle this by building models that are equivariant—meaning if you transform the input (rotate a molecule, permute nodes), the output transforms in the same predictable way. They use Riemannian spaces—curved surfaces where distance is measured differently—and hyperbolic spaces—weird surfaces where distances work differently—to reflect the actual structure of the data. They learn manifolds—the underlying low-dimensional shapes where data actually lives. These approaches make models more sample-efficient because they respect these structures instead of making the model learn them by accident.

papers.title: Adaptive Canonicalization with Application to Invariant Anisotropic Geometric Networks
papers.contribution: Admits universal approximation and outperforms data augmentation, standard canonicalization, and equivariant architectures on molecular, protein, and point cloud tasks.

papers.title: Equivariant Neural Networks for General Linear Symmetries on Lie Algebras
papers.contribution: Matches or outperforms strong equivariant and self-supervised baselines while using substantially fewer parameters and compute, with consistent improvements across diverse symmetry groups.

papers.title: G-Merging: Graph Models Merging for Parameter-Efficient Multi-Task Knowledge Consolidation
papers.contribution: G-Merging achieves performance close to or exceeding individual finetuned models while improving parameter efficiency across 8 graph downstream datasets.

papers.title: Guaranteed Simply Connected Mesh Reconstruction from an Unorganized Point Cloud
papers.contribution: Guarantees topological correctness while reconstructing mesh approximating input triangles on real and synthetic datasets.

papers.title: Intrinsic Lorentz Neural Network
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance and computational cost among hyperbolic models while consistently surpassing Euclidean baselines on CIFAR-10/100 and genomic benchmarks.

papers.title: Multi-Domain Transferable Graph Gluing for Building Graph Foundation Models
papers.contribution: GraphGlue demonstrates superior performance across diverse graph domains and empirically validates geometric scaling laws where larger datasets improve model transferability.

papers.title: SE(n)-Invariant Flow Matching: A General Framework with Application to Object Reassembly
papers.contribution: Improves accuracy on polygonal jigsaw puzzles and 3D fracture reassembly benchmarks through construction that factors out global pose at each timestep.

papers.title: The Natural Geometry of Code: Hyperbolic Representation Learning for Program Reasoning
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms Euclidean models (GraphCodeBERT) on code clone detection, completion, and link prediction, especially on tasks requiring deep structural understanding.

papers.title: <SO$G_k$>: One LLM Token for Explicit Graph Structural Understanding
papers.contribution: <SO$G_k$> achieves 9.9–41.4% performance improvement on five graph-level benchmarks with improved interpretability and consistency for graph understanding.

papers.title: Any-Subgroup Equivariant Networks via Symmetry Breaking
papers.contribution: A single network equivariant to multiple permutation subgroups outperforms both separate equivariant models and single non-equivariant models on symmetry selection, multitask, and transfer learning tasks.

papers.title: Are Common Substructures Transferable? Riemannian Graph Foundation Model with Neural Vector Bundles
papers.contribution: GAUGE demonstrates superior expressiveness in zero-shot link prediction and graph isomorphism tasks and validates transferability of graph substructures.

papers.title: DREAM: Dual-Standard Semantic Homogeneity with Dynamic Optimization for Graph Learning with Label Noise
papers.contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness across six graph datasets under three types of label noise against competing baselines, with rigorous theoretical analysis justifying the design.

papers.title: Discovering Symmetry Groups with Flow Matching
papers.contribution: LieFlow accurately discovers both continuous and discrete symmetries within unified framework, significantly outperforming LieGAN baseline on synthetic and real-world datasets.

papers.title: Fast Mixture of Curvature-Aware Experts for Diverse and Dynamic Graph Topologies
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods with average 27.5% speedup and 52.6% memory reduction from fast Riemannian attention applicable to general Transformer models.

papers.title: Feature-Aware (Hyper)graph Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance while uniquely scaling to featured large-scale graphs and hypergraphs.

papers.title: Global and Local Topology-Aware Graph Generation via Dual Conditioning Diffusion
papers.contribution: Substantially improves the quality of generated graphs by promoting joint modeling of global and local information, with consistent empirical validation across diverse graph generation tasks.

papers.title: HVAE: Hyperbolic Variational Autoencoder For Flexible Knowledge Transfer Across Multiple Domains
papers.contribution: Achieves superior performance particularly in scenarios with long-tail distributions and minimal domain overlap, enabling precise disentanglement of user intents.

papers.title: Interpretable Discovery of One-parameter Subgroups: A Modular Framework for Elliptical, Hyperbolic, and Parabolic Symmetries
papers.contribution: Identifies relevant continuous subgroups directly from data with guaranteed symmetry by construction across elliptic, hyperbolic, and parabolic regimes of matrix Lie groups including SO(n), SL(n), and Lorentz group.

papers.title: Large Scale Manifold Balanced Clustering
papers.contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness and scalability on benchmark datasets with theoretical analysis supporting balance maintenance.

papers.title: Learning Long Range Spatio-Temporal Representations over Continuous Time Dynamic Graphs with State Space Models
papers.contribution: CTDG-SSM achieves state-of-the-art on dynamic link prediction, node classification, and sequence classification with large gains on datasets requiring long-range temporal and spatial reasoning.

papers.title: MV-FGAD: Towards Efficient and Effective Federated Graph Anomaly Detection via Multi-view Learning
papers.contribution: Efficiently and effectively detects anomalies of varying strengths with efficiency and effectiveness across real-world datasets of varying types and scales.

papers.title: Mixtures of geodesic factor analyzers on Riemannian homogeneous spaces
papers.contribution: Substantially outperforms competing methods on spheres, shape spaces, and hyperbolic spaces with effectiveness demonstrated on corpus callosum and hippocampus shape analysis.

papers.title: RECON: Robust symmetry discovery via Explicit Canonical Orientation Normalization
papers.contribution: Enables unsupervised instance-level pose discovery, out-of-distribution pose detection, and plug-and-play improvement of pre-trained models without retraining.

papers.title: Reducing Symmetry Increase in Equivariant Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Proves increased symmetry admits infimum determined by feature space structure; validates theoretical predictions on synthetic and QM9 real-world dataset.

papers.title: Riemannian Networks over Full-Rank Correlation Matrices
papers.contribution: Demonstrates effectiveness of correlation manifold networks compared to existing SPD and Grassmannian approaches.

papers.title: Sheaves Reloaded: A Direction Awakening
papers.contribution: First SNN model with directional bias; consistently outperforms baselines on twelve real-world benchmarks.

papers.title: Structure-Centric Graph Foundation Model via Geometric Bases
papers.contribution: Modeling graphs as metric measure spaces, SCGFM introduces learnable geometric bases that define a shared structural coordinate system.

papers.title: Temporal Geometry of Deep Networks: Hyperbolic Representations of Training Dynamics for Intrinsic Explainability
papers.contribution: Hyperbolic temporal representations expose how structure emerges during training, offering intrinsic geometric explanations of self-organization in neural networks.

papers.title: Tensor learning with orthogonal, Lorentz, and symplectic symmetries
papers.contribution: Equivariant tensor models outperform non-equivariant baselines on materials science, theoretical computer science, and time series problems.

papers.title: TopoFormer: Topology Meets Attention for Graph Learning
papers.contribution: TopoFormer matches or exceeds strong GNN and topology-based baselines with predictable and efficient compute on graph classification and molecular prediction.

papers.title: VBA: Vector Bundle Attention for Intrinsically Geometric Representation Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on single-cell RNA sequencing benchmarks (outperforming Transformers by 3–5%), demonstrates superior performance on spatial transcriptomics, and validates competitive accuracy on 3D point clouds.
